data.title: Reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura — viva
data.summary: Pigmentary disorders · 5 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura** (Pigmentary disorders)_

**Q1. What is reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura (RAK)?**
- Rare autosomal dominant disorder (ADAM10 mutation) with reticulate, slightly depressed (atrophic) brown macules on the dorsa of hands and feet, appearing in childhood/adolescence and slowly spreading proximally; first described in Japan, reported from India

**Q2. Clinical features.**
- Angulated, freckle-like, slightly atrophic pigmented macules in a reticulate pattern on dorsa of hands and feet, extending to limbs, neck, face with age; darkens with sun
- Palmoplantar pits and breaks in dermatoglyphics (characteristic); no hypopigmentation; no systemic disease
- Overlap with Dowling–Degos disease reported

**Q3. Histopathology.**
- Thinned epidermis with elongated thin rete ridges, increased basal melanin and melanocytes, mild hyperkeratosis — like a 'mini Dowling–Degos'

**Q4. Enumerate reticulate pigmentary disorders and key differentials.**
- Dowling–Degos disease (flexural), reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura (dorsa of hands/feet with palmar pits), Galli–Galli disease (DDD + acantholysis), dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria (Dohi — acral hypo+hyperpigmented macules, ADAR1), dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria, Naegeli–Franceschetti–Jadassohn and dermatopathia pigmentosa reticularis (keratin 14, absent dermatoglyphics), dyskeratosis congenita (reticulate pigmentation, nail dystrophy, leukoplakia), X-linked reticulate pigmentary disorder, incontinentia pigmenti stage 3, confluent and reticulated papillomatosis, prurigo pigmentosa, macular amyloidosis, erythema ab igne, poikiloderma
- Key differentials for acral reticulate pigmentation: dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria (hypo + hyperpigmented, no pits), Dowling–Degos (flexural), Naegeli syndrome (no dermatoglyphics, hypohidrosis), acropigmentation of Dohi, freckles, lentigines

**Q5. Treatment.**
- No effective therapy; photoprotection; topical depigmenting agents and retinoids may lighten; Q-switched lasers variably helpful; reassurance and genetic counselling

## Quick spotter facts
- Reticulate atrophic pigmentation on dorsa of hands + palmar pits — Kitamura (ADAM10)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Reticulate pigmentary disorders). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
